questions.question: Why do you tell a lie? (Choose the best passive voice)
options: Why a lie is told by you?
Why is a lie be told by you?
Why is a lie being told by you?
questions.explanation: Simple present interrogative 'Why do you...' becomes 'Why + is/am/are + subject + V3 + by + agent?' -> 'Why is a lie told by you?' (Note: Option (a) in the paper is the closest intended match despite missing 'is').

questions.question: We are taught grammar by Mr. Singh. (Choose the best active voice)
questions.explanation: 'Are taught' is simple present passive, so the active voice uses simple present 'teaches'.

questions.question: I __________ here since morning. (Choose the correct tense form)
questions.explanation: With 'since morning' for an ongoing action up to the present, 'have been waiting' (present perfect continuous) is used.

questions.question: You have been riding non-stop for hours. You ________ be very tired. (Choose the correct auxiliary verb)
questions.explanation: 'Must' expresses strong logical deduction or certainty based on evidence.

questions.question: She ran out of the room. She was screaming. (Choose the correct combination)
options: She ran to the room screaming
She run out the room screaming
She had run to the room screaming
She ran out of the room screaming
questions.explanation: Using the present participle 'screaming' joins the simultaneous action accurately with 'ran out of the room'.

questions.question: ________ you mind standing up for a moment? (Choose the correct auxiliary verb)
questions.explanation: 'Would you mind + verb-ing' is the standard polite request structure.

questions.question: I ________ interested in metaphysics. (Choose the correct verb form)
questions.explanation: 'Have always been' expresses a state that started in the past and continues into the present.

questions.question: He said, "I have got a toothache". (Choose the correct indirect narration)
options: He says he has got a toothache.
He said he have a toothache.
He said that he had got a toothache.
He had said that he got a toothache.
questions.explanation: Reporting verb in past ('said') shifts 'have got' to 'had got' and 'I' to 'he'.

questions.question: She thanked me. (Choose the correct direct narration)
questions.explanation: 'Thanked me' in past tense corresponds to 'She said to me, "Thank you".'

questions.question: My brother did not ________ her. (Choose the meaningful expression)
questions.explanation: After 'did not', the base form (V1) of the verb 'choose' is used.

questions.question: ________ at a very high speed is dangerous. (Choose the meaningful expression)
questions.explanation: A gerund ('Driving') acts as the subject of the sentence before 'is dangerous'. (Note: Options in the scanned PDF print 'have written' etc. by typo; 'Driving' is the grammatical answer).

questions.question: She ________ six books on Indian Mythology. (Choose the meaningful expression)
questions.explanation: Singular subject 'She' takes 'has written'.

questions.question: This material is different ________ that. (Choose the correct preposition)
questions.explanation: 'Different from' is the standard preposition used to show contrast or distinction.

questions.question: He climbed ________ the ladder. (Choose the correct preposition)
questions.explanation: We climb 'on' or 'up' a ladder; among the given choices, 'on' is correct.

questions.question: He has been absent ________ Monday. (Choose the correct preposition)
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used before a specific point in time like 'Monday'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:
options: Sid can play Tennis as good as his brother.
Sid will play Tennis is well as his brother.
Sid can play Tennis as well as his brother.
Sid has played Tennis as good as his brother.
questions.explanation: 'As well as' correctly uses the adverb 'well' to modify the verb 'play'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:
options: I have a home work to do
I have home work to do.
I will have home work to do.
I having home work to do.
questions.explanation: 'Homework' is an uncountable noun, so 'a homework' is incorrect; 'I have homework to do.' is correct.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:
options: That may be sure a mistake.
questions.explanation: The adverb 'surely' properly modifies the clause/verb.

questions.question: He ________ if we had taken our food. (Choose the best option)
questions.explanation: 'Had taken' in the dependent clause aligns with past tense 'asked'.

questions.question: All depends on ________ the examination. (Choose the best option)
questions.explanation: After the preposition 'on', 'his passing' (possessive determiner + gerund) is grammatically correct.

questions.question: You ________ not go to attend the meeting. (Choose the best option)
questions.explanation: 'Need not' expresses lack of necessity or obligation.

questions.question: When Radha ________ back, she will sleep. (Choose the best option)
questions.explanation: In time clauses starting with 'when' referring to the future, simple present ('comes') is used while the main clause uses 'will sleep'.

questions.question: Would you mind ________ to my house, please? (Choose the best option)
questions.explanation: 'Would you mind' is followed by a gerund ('coming').

questions.question: She is ________ most beautiful girl. (Choose the best article)
questions.explanation: Definite article 'the' precedes the superlative degree 'most beautiful'.

questions.question: My sister ________ a dress for her birthday last week. (Choose the best option)
questions.explanation: 'Last week' indicates completed past action, requiring the past tense 'bought'.

questions.question: Kamlesh has been ________ his house for a few days. (Choose the best option)
questions.explanation: 'Has been' is followed by the present participle 'repairing' in the present perfect continuous tense.

questions.question: Sita fell ________ the rickshaw. (Choose the best option)
questions.explanation: 'Fell off' means moving downward and away from a surface or vehicle such as a rickshaw.

questions.question: You can do it ________. (Choose the best option)
questions.explanation: The reflexive pronoun corresponding to 'You' is 'yourself'.

questions.question: Choose the correct spelling:
questions.explanation: 'Families' is the correct plural spelling of 'family'.

questions.question: What time does the bus ________ central London? (Choose the best option)
questions.explanation: 'Leave for' is used when stating a destination toward which a journey begins.

questions.question: 'There is a house now far away where once I received love' - is from the poem:
questions.explanation: This opening line belongs to 'My Grandmother's House' by Kamala Das.

questions.question: The Soldier is a ________ poem. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'The Soldier' by Rupert Brooke is a patriotic war poem/sonnet.

questions.question: Kamala Das is ________ poetess. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: Kamala Das is a prominent Indian English poetess and writer.

questions.question: 'Fire-Hymn' is composed by (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'Fire-Hymn' is written by Keki N. Daruwala.

questions.question: 'I celebrate myself and sing myself' - is written by (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: This is the opening line of 'Song of Myself' by Walt Whitman.

questions.question: The word drama comes from a ________ word. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: The word 'drama' comes from a Greek word meaning 'action' or 'deed'.

questions.question: The snake looked at the poet ________. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: In D.H. Lawrence's poem 'Snake', the snake lifted its head and mused/looked vaguely.

questions.question: The speaker in 'Fire-Hymn' belongs to ________ religion. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: K.N. Daruwala belonged to the Zoroastrian (Parsi) religion.

questions.question: Macavity is full of ________. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: In T.S. Eliot's poem, Macavity is a master criminal full of deceitfulness.

questions.question: 'The Scholar Gipsy' has been written by (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'The Scholar-Gipsy' is a famous poem by Matthew Arnold.

questions.question: Seibei was a twelve year old ________ boy. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: In Shiga Naoya's story 'The Artist', Seibei is a twelve-year-old Japanese boy.

questions.question: Our ancestors enjoyed ________ Rule. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: In 'Indian Civilization and Culture', Mahatma Gandhi states our ancestors enjoyed true 'Home Rule'.

questions.question: Martin Luther King dislikes ________ discrimination. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: Martin Luther King Jr. fought against racial discrimination in America.

questions.question: Lomov is a man of ________ temperament. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: In Anton Chekhov's 'A Marriage Proposal', Ivan Vassilevitch Lomov is a hypochondriac of nervous temperament.

questions.question: Bertrand Russell was a philosopher and a ________. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: Bertrand Russell was a renowned British philosopher, logician, and mathematician.

questions.question: ________ is called the father of the modern novel. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: Henry Fielding is widely regarded as the father of the English/modern novel.

questions.question: ________ were rulers of ancient Egypt. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: Pharaohs were the monarchs/rulers of ancient Egypt.

questions.question: Pearl S. Buck is an ________ writer. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: Pearl S. Buck was an American writer who wrote 'India Through a Traveller's Eyes'.

questions.question: 'I Have a Dream' is a speech delivered by ________. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: 'I Have a Dream' was delivered by Martin Luther King Jr. in 1963.

questions.question: Nanukaka was the narrator's ________. (Choose the correct option)
questions.explanation: In 'A Pinch of Snuff' by Manohar Malgonkar, Nanukaka is the narrator's maternal uncle.

questions.question: Write an essay in about 150-200 words on any one: (a) Environmental Preservation (b) Women Empowerment (c) Demonetisation (d) A Village Fair (e) The Happiest Day of my life
questions.explanation: Subjective essay writing question (150-200 words).

questions.question:
Explain any two of the following:
(a) The ways of managing childbirth in traditional societies are many and varied.
(b) It is obvious that we know more than animals do, and it is common to consider this one of our advantages.
(c) Religion is ever present in Indian life, in its best as well as in its worst aspect.
questions.explanation: (a) From 'A Child is Born' by Germaine Greer. (b) From 'Ideas that Have Helped Mankind' by Bertrand Russell. (c) From 'India Through a Traveller's Eyes' by Pearl S. Buck.

questions.question:
Explain any one of the following:
(a) Here lies a most beautiful lady. Light of step and heart was she;
(b) Broken, yet rebellious, I swore this time To save it from the sin of forgiving
(c) The voice of my education said to me He must be killed
questions.explanation: (a) From 'An Epitaph' by Walter de la Mare. (b) From 'Fire-Hymn' by K.N. Daruwala. (c) From 'Snake' by D.H. Lawrence.

questions.question: Write a letter to your sister, in about 100 words, asking her to visit your place in the holidays. OR Write a letter to your headmaster in about 100 words, asking him for permission to use the library after school hours.
questions.explanation: Subjective informal/formal letter writing question (~100 words).

questions.question:
Answer in about 40 to 50 words, any five of the following:
(a) What is civilization in the real sense of the term?
(b) Why is Zakir Hussain overwhelmed?
(c) In what dress did the author go to the Minister along with Nanukaka?
(d) What does Martin Luther say about the life of Negroes?
(e) What are the dramatic structures of a tragedy?
(f) Name two works of Shakespeare.
(g) Why and how did the snake come out of the hole?
(h) Why is Macavity called a criminal?
questions.explanation: Short answer questions (40-50 words each, any 5). Examples: (f) Hamlet, Macbeth.

questions.question: Write the summary of any one of the poems: (i) Snake (ii) Fire-Hymn OR Write the summary of any one of the prose pieces: (i) The Artist (ii) A Child is Born
questions.explanation: Subjective summary writing question.

questions.question: Write a note on American English. OR What are the difficulties faced by Indians in learning English?
questions.explanation: Subjective short note question on Story of English.

questions.question:
Translate any five of the following sentences into English:
(i) हमेशा सच बोलो।
(ii) जाड़े के बाद वसंत ऋतु आती है।
(iii) कल मेरी भेंट राजन से हुई।
(iv) सच्चा मित्र संसार में दुर्लभ है।
(v) वह कई वर्षों से घर नहीं आया है।
(vi) वह एक अच्छा तैराक है।
(vii) भारत का इतिहास गौरवशाली है।
questions.explanation: (i) Always speak the truth. (ii) Spring comes after winter. (iii) I met Rajan yesterday. (iv) A true friend is rare in the world. (v) He has not come home for many years. (vi) He is a good swimmer. (vii) The history of India is glorious.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions:
Sarojini Naidu was educated in her early years under her father's own care. He wanted her to become a great mathematician or scientist, but she loved to dream and write poems. She was hardly eleven when she wrote her first poem. At nineteen she wrote a long poem in the manner of famous English poets. After her matriculation in India, she went to England for higher education. She met Sir Edmund who was a distinguished man of letters. He was impressed by her knowledge and intelligence. He was surprised to see that she had written poems in flawless English but felt disappointed to find that they had nothing of the East in them. He advised her to write something about her own country and from then onwards, she devoted herself to writing verses about India.
Questions: (i) What did Sarojini Naidu's father want her to choose as a career? (ii) What did Sir Edmund advise Sarojini Naidu? (iii) Why was he disappointed by her poems? (iv) What did he advise her? Did she follow his advice?
OR Write a precis of the passage on small events in human life and give a suitable title.
questions.explanation: Comprehension answers: (i) Mathematician or scientist. (ii)-(iv) He was disappointed that her poems had nothing Eastern in them, advised her to write about India, and she followed his advice. Precis title: Importance of Small Things.
